name: FHIR Clinical CDR
summary: An open, portable FHIR resource-store accelerator for MongoDB with standard APIs, transparent storage, and explainable search.
description: Imports FHIR JSON, Bundle, and NDJSON data into a reviewed strategy-owned database, preserves canonical resources, materializes mandatory operational search projections, and exposes FHIR read/write/search workflows with visible FHIR Search to MQL compilation.

strategy.description: FHIR database, generation, and search configuration

ui.status_message: Implemented: FHIR R5/R6 resource catalog, JSON/Bundle/NDJSON import, bundled structural and base-schema validation, mandatory search and compartment projection, mandatory indexes, synthetic generation, CapabilityStatement, create/update, read, type search, and FHIR Search-to-MQL explain. History, transactions, conditional operations, subscriptions, terminology validation, profile conformance, and SMART authorization are not implemented.
ui.story:
Teams moving a FHIR workload to MongoDB usually agree that resources fit the document model, but they still need proof that the result behaves like a usable FHIR system: familiar APIs, predictable identity, declared validation, searchable resources, and a migration path they can inspect. A database layout alone does not provide that confidence.

This accelerator supplies the reusable kernel for that middle ground. Canonical FHIR R5 or R6 resources remain recognizable, each configured resource type is isolated in its own collection, and operational search projections sit beside the resource for efficient MongoDB execution. Healthcare Data Lab then exposes the complete journey: inspect the metamodel, import or generate data, compile FHIR Search to MQL, execute it against the tenant database, and inspect the result.

The goal is portability and extension rather than claiming to be a finished commercial FHIR server. Customers and partners can use the kernel as a foundation for real migrations, add the conformance, security, history, terminology, and operational controls their product requires, and keep the storage and query behavior visible.
ui.how_it_works:
The activated strategy configuration selects one of the bundled R5 or R6 packages. The import boundary accepts a resource, Bundle, or NDJSON batch; rejects resource types outside both the Clinical CDR recipe scope and bundled fhir-mql configuration; removes client-supplied operational fields; validates at the selected supported level; and computes mandatory `_search` and `_compartments` projections through fhir-mql.

The storage adapter routes each resource by `resourceType` to a prefixed MongoDB collection and uses the pair `(resourceType, id)` as logical identity. Canonical JSON stays at the document root. `_search` and `_compartments` remain directly indexable siblings, while Kehrnel-owned control metadata is grouped under `_kehrnel`; MongoDB retains its own `_id`. The stored-document schema version, global projection-contract version, and per-resource projection version are stripped from FHIR responses together with the operational projections; valid FHIR primitive-extension fields are preserved. Search projections, compartment materialization, and configured indexes cannot be disabled for stored data.

At query time, the compiler resolves the search parameters supported for the selected resource type and returns the MongoDB collection, filter, sort, limit, and offset. Unknown or unsupported parameters fail closed in strict mode. Runtime capability and index operations derive their facts from the bundled fhir-mql and fhir-gen packages instead of a broader release-wide claim.
benefits: Canonical FHIR JSON remains readable and round-trippable; a narrow, documented operational projection is removed from FHIR-facing responses.
The per-resource-type collection family matches FHIR identity and allows search projections and indexes to evolve independently by resource type.
FHIR Search compilation is visible before execution, so teams can inspect the generated MQL and test whether configured indexes serve their real query shapes.
The activated R5 or R6 release and package-backed resource catalogs make the implemented scope explicit.
The same kernel supports guided learning, migration rehearsal, synthetic data, and tenant-backed operational experimentation without locking the workload to a managed cloud API.
ui.ideal_for: This strategy is a good fit for teams migrating an existing FHIR integration or data service to MongoDB, building a portable FHIR data foundation, evaluating MongoDB against real FHIR search patterns, or creating a partner product that needs an extensible resource-store kernel. It is especially useful when the team wants to own its infrastructure and application behavior while retaining familiar FHIR APIs and an inspectable MongoDB implementation.
ui.consider_alternatives: Choose a complete FHIR server or managed FHIR service when the project requires broad specification conformance, version history, transactions, conditional interactions, subscriptions, terminology services, implementation-guide and profile validation, SMART authorization, or a supported production platform out of the box. This accelerator is appropriate when teams want a portable MongoDB foundation and intend to own or partner on the remaining product and operational layers. Its conformance claim is limited to the interactions and resource types reported by the active CapabilityStatement.

index_contract.identityIndex: A unique ascending index on `id` is enforced by the storage adapter in each materialized resource collection.
index_contract.searchIndexSource: The active fhir-mql resource configuration supplies resource-specific index definitions to `fhir_ensure_indexes`.
index_contract.summary: Search indexes are runtime-resolved because supported resource types, search parameters, and field projections vary by FHIR release and active configuration. The manifest therefore documents the contract and source of truth rather than duplicating a static index list that can drift.

cards.title: Querying
cards.body: FHIR Search parameters supported for the selected resource type are compiled to MongoDB MQL by fhir-mql. The lab shows the collection, filter, controls, ignored parameters, and execution summary.

cards.title: Migration import
cards.body: FHIR R5/R6 JSON, Bundle entries, and NDJSON are checked against the activated release and bundled resource configuration, projected into operational fields, and persisted through the tenant-bound storage adapter. Large migrations should use bounded NDJSON chunks.

cards.title: Synthetic Generation
cards.body: fhir-gen recipes create representative FHIR datasets for the active release. Every stored resource passes through the same validation, projection, versioning, and index contract as imported data.

cards.title: Schema & Indexes
cards.body: The logical-id index and resource-specific fhir-mql search indexes are mandatory. The catalog exposes the stored-document and projection versions used to identify targeted rebuilds.
